extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners admitted to practice before the USPTO; respondents in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO final order imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) based on disbarment in another jurisdiction and setting out procedural requirements, sanctions, publication, and obligations for the respondent during exclusion and on reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the Director may impose reciprocal discipline (here: exclusion) based on disciplinary action by another jurisdiction (District of Columbia Court of Appeals disbarring Respondent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order informed Respondent that the OED Director had filed a Complaint requesting exclusion identical to the discipline imposed by the other jurisdiction. If Respondent seeks to contest imposition of exclusion pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), Respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based on any grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). The Director determines whether there is a genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was excluded for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) as a consequence of being disbarred for violations of the Rules of Professional Conduct in connection with handling a client's funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Notice summarizes the other-jurisdiction findings that support the §10.23 violations: receipt and deposit of a client's check in excess of $240,000 into Respondent's account; failure to notify the client of receipt or deposit; taking and spending the entirety of the check knowing the funds did not belong to him; willful professional misconduct characterized as theft, dishonesty, misappropriation, failure to notify client of receipt of funds, failure to segregate funds, failure to deposit funds in separate account, and failure to inform a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director orders that Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office, beginning on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion is the primary reciprocal sanction imposed in this proceeding pursuant to the cited statutes and regulations (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up client matters and restrictions during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after that date to wind up client business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the 30 days of limited recognition Respondent is directed to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40. Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 10.40
rubrics_metrics.description: While exercising limited recognition to wind up matters, Respondent must withdraw from employment in pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically directs Respondent to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings pursuant to the requirements of § 10.40 (procedural/ethical duties on withdrawal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion and reasons for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes a sample NOTICE OF EXCLUSION summarizing the factual findings and disciplinary grounds. Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to other disciplinary authorities under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires transmittal of notice to other jurisdictions and courts as provided by § 11.59, to ensure reciprocal awareness of sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations while excluded and on reinstatement (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded and shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explicitly commands compliance with § 11.58 (requirements while excluded) and § 11.60 (requirements and procedures for reinstatement), indicating ongoing duties and conditions for seeking readmission to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/notification and record of mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service certifying that the Final Order was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at addresses provided to OED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document records dates and addresses used for service and demonstrates the procedural requirement to serve disciplinary orders on the respondent and to document service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites the statutory and regulatory bases authorizing the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline and to publish and notify other authorities of the discipline.
